newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank holds interest rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank holds interest rates steady.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.

The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was held at three percent for the next three weeks.

The outcome of the meeting was in line with economists' expectations that rates will be held steady for some time. German money supply data released earlier on Thursday dampened lingering hopes for an easing later this year.

The Bundesbank said M3 money supply grew at a stronger than expected annualised rate of 8.7 percent in August, up from 8.6 percent in July. The growth rates have been consistently above the Bundesbank seven percent target ceiling so far this year.
M3 money supply is the Bundesbank's main monetary policy indicator.
The Bundesbank, which has regularly set its repo rate for the next two weeks in advance at its recent council meetings, held it steady for three weeks this time around.
It will not hold its next regular meeting until October 10 as there is a German public holiday in two week's time.
